Wind · "Elements" direction — the Reference System

Reference system
and screens, v2

One single rule of form, applied everywhere. 24-unit grid, 2-unit stroke, clean ends, sharp joints, integer coordinates — no optical correction anywhere in the system. The disc has only one use: it says state. Color never decorates; it says element at the mark, and state everywhere else. A short, living theme table (V7/A94) — Elements, drawn from the colors set around the Wind icon, and Innamoramento, drawn from two CE colors, each in light and dark. This document is generated from the glyph catalogue: it cannot show a drawing different from the one that is measured.

NORMATIVE — Wind's Reference System (A18: what it draws is shipped, what is shipped is drawn here — the gate checks it both ways, traces included). Adopted on 2026-08-24 (PLAN-ELEMENTS, CE decision D1): it replaces the "Clarity / Wada" System — archived at docs/archives/systeme.v1.dc.html — at the path read by e2e/system-coherence.mjs and e2e/contrast.mjs. This document is THE source, hand-edited (DC-D2: any commit that touches the UI amends it in the same commit); the study generator stays frozen as a trace (spikes/direction-elements/v2/). The A1–A78 amendment log is carried over in full and verbatim — these are dated facts, they are not rewritten — adoption decisions are recorded under the reference V-n (series closed at V14), and amendments continue the A-n series (A79–). One arbitration of form: this document carries its colors as CSS tokens rather than inline styles, which lets it switch theme in O(1) and forbids it from writing a hex value anywhere but in the contract table. The cost is real: the canvas editor handles poorly what it cannot see inline, and element-by-element editing suffers for it. The choice is deliberate — a two-polarity System cannot prove itself with copied-in colors.

Principles

Two gestures from Japan already guided this direction; v2 adds a third, borrowed from the Elements icon set. They are not ornaments: they explain every rule of the system, and they agree — all three say the same thing, remove rather than add.

Omotenashi, hospitality

Anticipate, then step back

The host prepares everything in advance and removes what clutters, so the guest has nothing to ask for. From this come the rule of four actions at most, the server that configures itself, and the two visual choices offered once at onboarding, never asked again.

Takumi, the craftsman

Precision through restraint

The master reaches precision by removing, never by adding. From this come the single 1 px rule, the single accent, the single elevation, and since V14 the sharp corner. Every stroke carries an intention; nothing is decorative. The material is warm, the shadow leans toward ink.

The single rule (v2)

One shape only, zero arbitration

The Elements icon set contains not a single optical correction: markers are placed on the geometric center of their container, and a single distance is decided across the whole system — the one that offsets the Stone disc — because it has a numbered reason. v2 carries the doctrine over line by line: whatever cannot be derived from a dimension is removed, or justified in writing.

What v2 removes to hold these three principles together: the hitofude stroke (A28/A36/A40), the panel background --panel, the 26 surplus Wada themes (A42), the icon font, the round avatar, and the solid unread dot. Each of these removals is recorded in the log, with what it costs.

↑ Top of document

Brand

Wind is the mail and calendar tool of the Elements suite (“what the wind carries, the rhythm of days”). The suite sets the rule: the icon says the function, the disc says the element. Wind's mark is an envelope on a tile, whose flap is a teal half-disc — it is the only oriented shape in the whole set, and it is placed by tangency, never by optical correction: the flat side of the half-disc is tangent to the top inner edge of the envelope. The corner “W” badge disappears (V1): the set never puts anything in a corner container, and the “W” restated what the name already said.

The construction

24 grid, solid tile #F2EDE3, structure #141414, stroke 2.3 at master tier. Envelope M4 8h16v9H4z — four whole coordinates. Flap: half-disc of radius 3.25, of surface area strictly equal to the solid disc of radius 2.3 that marks the other five tools of the suite. The tile's radius is a platform ratio — 15/64 at any size, 23 px here. Since V14 it is the only rounded shape that remains in the whole product, and it does not belong to us: the OS dictates it.

The variants — fixed across themes (W-D3)

64 48 32 24 16

Three tiers, like the suite: the 16 tier (16 grid, solid 2 px bars), the 24 tier (2.0 stroke on whole coordinates) and the master (2.3 stroke, from 29 px up). Teal #1F8A8A and tile #F2EDE3 are the only colors of the brand; they are what gave this v2 its two palettes, and they do not vary in any theme. The application's 16 tier is not drawn — the V9 debt.

Two regimes, one statement (V11)

Wind

As tile — app icon, welcome screen, migration modal — the mark is fixed: structure #141414, tile #F2EDE3, teal #1F8A8A, identical in both polarities. As glyph — the header, the drawer — it follows the current ink and --brand. This is not a breach of W-D3, it is its boundary: the tile carries its own ground, a bare glyph has none, and a fixed #141414 set on a dark background would be invisible (1.04:1). The rule is therefore stated in two parts, and the document says which one applies where.

The signature — what replaces the hitofude stroke (V2)

at rest during a cycle

The calligraphic stroke has no place in an entirely constructed system: it is dead (A28, A36 and A40 fall — the SMIL discovery in the mask with them). It is replaced by the disc / ring pair, which is already the grammar of the set: the solid disc denotes a goal reached, the hollow ring the same disc being reached. Same diameter, Ø 9 px, same token --brand; the ring is not one shape more, it is the disc with a 2 px wall and its top quarter open — without that gap, the rotation would not be visible. Two locations: to the left of the status bar, and at the top of the migration modal. With prefers-reduced-motion, the ring stops and stays hollow. This is a loss: the stroke had cost several jobs.

Pitted against six others, and confirmed (2026-08-24): pulsing, alternation solid ↔ hollow, square at an eighth turn, four corners, sweep, brand flap — all drawn and animated at actual size. Two break a rule (A8, A52), three put a container where the round says the state, one strips its orientation from the only oriented shape of the set. The ring is the only one of the seven that adds neither shape, nor color, nor value — see V2 for the detail of what was set aside, and why.

Colors

Seventeen roles, as in the delivered System — but no longer quite the same ones: --panel is dead (V3, the single background and the rule do everything) and --brand is born (V1, the exact teal of the icon set, component and never text). Every color goes through a token; no hex is written anywhere but this table — with three named exceptions: the two fixed colors of the tile mark (V1/V11), the twenty-four hues of the marker swatch (A74), and the two values that mail-render bakes into the body of an email (A61).

Why two teals. The #1F8A8A of the icon set holds 3.70:1 on the light background: compliant for a disc, a rule or a focus ring (threshold 3), not compliant for text (threshold 4.5). It is therefore kept exact as --brand and split off into an ink --accent #1A7A7A — same hue, minimal lightness, the A8 remedy — which holds 5.11:1 on the surface. The brand never carries a word; the accent never carries a disc.

Two values of the raw palette were corrected to the minimum, at constant hue, before entering this table: the muted text #6E7577 → #606668 (4.19:1 → 5.21:1) and the rule #E3E3DD → #CBC8BB (1.15:1 → 1.50:1). The rule's threshold is not invented: it is the rule Wind already ships. In an airy document 1.15:1 holds; in a list where the rule is the only row separator, it disappears.

A hardening taken deliberately. A28 declares rules "decorative, outside the thresholds of the bench: only text is measured". This v2 measures them anyway, with as threshold the rule actually shipped by Clarity — because V3 kills --panel and makes the rule the only pane separator. A rule that carried a background as backup could stay decorative; a rule that carries alone can no longer.

Color themes

The theme table is short and living (V7 amended by A94, CE decision of 2026-08-29 / ADR 0027: themes can be added or removed from time to time — never the return of a twenty-eight-row table). Four themes: "Elements" — the default, with no attribute — and "Innamoramento" (born "Mona", renamed at A95), each with its dark variant, identifier suffixed -nuit. The fourteen Wada combinations and their fourteen night variants stay removed (V7). Elements comes from the colors laid around the Wind icon — the tile #F2EDE3 becomes --tile, the teal #1F8A8A becomes --brand, and the rest is composed around them. Innamoramento comes from two CE colors — the accent #AD204C, the tile hue #A0868F split by polarity (A94). The "Automatic dark" setting shows the -nuit variant of the chosen theme when the system's dark setting is on; the base theme is the only value persisted, the suffix is a derived state.

A rule came out of this bench. The pinned row has --tile for a floor, and the accent there is worth only 4.38:1 in light — above the threshold for a component (3), below the one for text (4.5). Hence the ban, written and measured: on the tile, the accent only serves as a hairline and a focus ring, never as a label. The other four inks pass there without reservation.

The account markers' swatch set (A74, amended A82) — twelve hues, two polarities

These are content colors, not theme tokens: they don't follow direction, they are measured against it. A fact re-derived at the bench: no single hue holds 3:1 on both the light background and the night background — so each family lives in two variants, the dark one served in the light theme (white glyph), the light one in the night theme (glyph #1c1b1b), through .rep[data-teinte] exactly like system.css — where the 24 hex values live as tokens --mk-<hue> since A82, because each hex serves twice. Two uses: the badge, 20 px, Settings only (account row and the choice swatch set — the background carries the hue, the glyph crosses it), and the stroke — the hue as the bare glyph's color — 16 px in the nav, 14 px in the header row and in the reading pane (A80/A82). The glyph shown below is arbitrary and identical across every row: the hue and the glyph are chosen separately, no pairing is imposed. The hue is measured on the five backgrounds it sits on — the row (bg, sel, hover, tile), the card and the Settings rail (surface) — the same table holding for the badge and for the stroke.

The suite's palette does not survive the two-theme system, and it's measured. The six element hues of the icon set, laid as a bare disk on the five row backgrounds: Wind 3.33 / 3.26 ✓ · Stone 3.23 / 3.37 ✓ · River 6.01 / 1.81 ✗ · Flame 3.81 / 2.85 ✗ · Helios 1.65 / 6.60 ✗ · Moon 5.26 / 2.07 ✗. Helios doesn't hold up on paper: in its icon, it's the #141414 that surrounds it that manufactures its contrast; laid bare, it goes dead. That is why the markers' swatch set stays A74's, measured, and not the suite's palette.

Typography

System font. Authority is graded by size, not by weight. v2 adds a display register borrowed from the icon document (V6): weight 340, letter-spacing -.03em, reserved for the two largest sizes — the conversation title and the home hero. Everywhere else, nothing changes: 400, 500 or 600.

SizeRole Weight / line-heightSample
11 pxSection eyebrow, card title, nav sections 600 · letter-spacing .2em · caps Boxes
12 pxMeta, timestamp, counters, status bar, field label (caps, .1em) 400 to 600 · tabular figures 09:12  Subject
13 pxList preview, controls, info chips 400 · 1.45 I picked up articles 4 and 7 after our exchange.
14 pxSubject in the message list (unread at weight 700) 400 / 700 · 1.3 Review of the Vantis contract
15 pxMessage body, expanded sender name, invitation title 400 / 600 · 1.65 The renewal clause still needs settling.
16 pxMailbox title (list banner), the word "Wind" 600 · 1.3 Inbox
24 pxConversation title, reading pane — display register 340 · 1.2 · -.03em Review of the Vantis contract
40 pxHome hero, single use — display register 340 · 1.05 · -.03em Your address

The display register calls for a variable font ("Segoe UI Variable Display" on Windows, Wind's target). The fallback is explicit and documented: on a platform without a variable font, weight 340 falls back to 400 — the title stays a title, it is never bold. No drawing depends on the weight.

↑ Top of document

Title truncation

A title — subject in the list, reading-pane title, or conversation title — never wraps: past the available width, it truncates on a single line with a trailing ellipsis, like the preview. Row height stays constant and alignment stays regular; the full title remains readable in the reading pane.

Applied

Camille Rousseau09:12 Review of the Vantis contract and its second-half fee schedules The renewal clause still needs settling.

A single line, ellipsis at the end. The row keeps its height; the subject and the preview cut off the same way.

To avoid

Camille Rousseau09:12 Review of the Vantis contract and its second-half fee schedules The renewal clause still needs settling.

A title that wraps makes row height vary and breaks the vertical rhythm of the list — and it also breaks windowing, which counts on fixed-size templates.

↑ Top of document

Shapes, elevation, signature

Wind stays flat (V3): no card, no shadow in the list, nor in navigation, nor in the reading pane. The icon document is made of bordered panels at radius 18 — v2 does not carry them over: on the screen of a dense mail client, cards everywhere turn back into a web page. Only objects — a message, an invitation, a notice — sit on paper; and only the first three are elevated.

Zero radius — and two shapes that aren't

CR

Zero radius (V14). Surfaces, controls, tiles: sharp corners everywhere, in this document as in the product. The rule fits in one sentence, and it checks out at a glance.

Two round shapes remain, and they are not radii: the disc (50%) says state — unread, cycle — and the switch handle, and the pill (999) says the slide, on the switch's own track alone. An account's identity, for its part, is now said in letters (A80) and in a stroke (A82) — no longer by a round shape. These are the only round things in the system, and that is what gives them their force: V4 had made the disc round only halfway, V14 goes all the way.

One exception, declared and permanent: the radius of the application icon (15/64) is a platform dimension, outside the system — it is the OS that dictates it. The three tokens --r-surface / --r-control / --r-tile remain: they hold the rule in the eye's place — there is no longer a single radius literal left to write.

One elevation

0 2px 8px rgba(25,29,30,0.08) in light, 0 2px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.40) in dark. Warm shadow, never gray. Reserved for the thread's message cards, the compose card, the notice slot, the toast, and the active row of the Settings rail. The reading pane and screen 03 are flat: never an enclosing elevation; the invitation card does not elevate either, it belongs to the flow of the content.

The disc says state — and nothing else (V4)

unread cycle PM identity 4 account

Ø 9 px, in --brand, two uses: a row's unread marker and the status bar's indicator. To give it back its uniqueness, two round shapes are removed: the initials avatar becomes a square (tile, sharp corner since V14) and the solid unread badge in navigation becomes a number in tabular figures, in the accent color. Since A82, the disc is the only round shape on screen 02 — measured across the whole window: the marker dot has left the nav for a bare stroke. It survives at Settings — a choice dot, not an identity mark; it keeps its glyph there for V5's reason (A8: never color alone).

Symmetric margins (A33)

Reply contract.pdf

In every chip, every button, every tab, the content is margined identically on the left and right: a single horizontal padding (12 px for chips, 14 px for buttons and tabs). A leading or trailing icon never shrinks the margin on its side.

No optical correction

The icon set's own rule applies to the interface: a marker sits on the geometric center of its container, never by eye. The unread disc is centered on the whole row — a bare row or a row carrying chips — by construction, in flex, and not by an offset tuned by hand. A distance that cannot be derived from a dimension gets removed, or is justified in writing in this document.

The rule, unique

1 px, --border, everywhere, without exception. Since V3 it alone carries the separation between panes, the header boundary, and the status bar boundary — the panel background no longer helps it. It also borders the initials tile, which without it would not exist. Measured: 1.50:1 on the light background, 1.66:1 on the dark background, 1.44:1 on the light tile.

↑ Top of document

Corners

Zero radius. Surfaces, controls, tiles, cards, modals, chips, fields, tabs, navigation rows, application window: sharp corners everywhere, in this document as in the product. Two round shapes remain, and each says something — the disc (state; identity left it with A82) and the switch's pill (the slide). One single exception, declared and permanent: the application icon, whose radius is a platform dimension. This is verdict V14; here is what established it, and what it costs.

Field-validated 2026-08-24 Finding by the Chief Engineer on the actual rendering of the document; the platform idiom will be re-checked at the first application window delivered.

1 · What the guidance does — measured, not assumed

The drawings are strictly sharp-cornered. The 91 glyphs, 277 sub-paths, 746 path commands (re-measured on the catalogue's d paths, 2026-08-30): zero rounded corner, stroke-linejoin: miter and stroke-linecap: butt everywhere, without a single exception.

The documents that present them are rounded — and undisciplined. The glyph sheet and the icon set together use eight different radii: 18, 16, 14, 12, 11, 10, 9 and 2 px, plus the pill. These are presentation pages, not a system: they could not serve as a model for the grammar of containers.

The guidance thus had a strict grammar for what it draws and none for what it contains. A decision was needed — copying it would not have been consistency, but an inheritance of disorder.

2 · What decided it: V4's argument, taken all the way

V4 had given the initials tile a 2 px radius for a precise reason: at 6 px it became frankly round and stole the disc's uniqueness of meaning. The argument was good, and it was only half applied. If roundness carries meaning, then every rounded container dilutes it: a card at 10, a button at 6, and a tile at 2 were three degrees of roundness that said nothing.

Zero radius. Two round shapes, and they say something: the disc (state — since A82 it says only that) and the pill (the slide).

The rule is shorter than the one it replaces — "three radii, no other value" — and it checks out at a glance. It is V3's gesture, which killed --panel to let the rule line do the work: here, radii are killed to let roundness carry the meaning. And it is Takumi: remove, don't add.

3 · What it costs — stated, not glossed over

Windows 11 rounds everything. Wind targets Windows — Segoe UI Variable, WebView2, Tauri — and Fluent rounds windows, menus, fields, and buttons. A sharp-cornered application might read there as foreign to its platform. That was the only serious argument against it, and it could not be judged from a sheet.

Field finding of 2026-08-24: this document rendered in the browser, viewed on a real screen — sharp corners validated, kept. The reservation is named: what was looked at was the document, not an application window set next to the system's own applications. The Fluent idiom will be re-checked at the first window delivered. If it says otherwise, the reversal fits in one line — put 10 / 6 / 2 back into the three shape tokens. That is why they exist, and they stay.

The application icon stays rounded — 15/64, a platform dimension. It becomes the only rounded shape in the entire product, at its most-looked-at point. A declared, permanent, and visible exception.

Elevation carries the sharp corner less well: a cast shadow under a right angle is seen more than it is felt. Low cost — the system elevates at only five places.

The four shapes in the last row — disc, ring, dot, pill — do not move from one column to the other, and that is the point: they are not radii, they are shapes that carry meaning. In the kept column, they are the only round things in the system. The gauge has left this row: a progress bar is not a meaning-bearing shape but a container — it went sharp-cornered along with the rest.

5 · How the rule holds

Through three shape tokens — --r-surface, --r-control, --r-tile — declared on html and not on :root: they do not depend on polarity, and the color-token contract must not be inflated by them. There is no longer a single radius literal left to write anywhere in the system: "no other value" stops being a rule obeyed by hand and becomes a rule that can no longer be broken by carelessness. The toggle that served for arbitration has been removed: a System that offers two states of its own rule is a System that has not decided.

↑ Top of document

Icons

The entire set is drawn, not composed: 91 inline SVG glyphs, 24 grid, 2-unit stroke, butt caps, miter joins, integer coordinates. The Material Symbols font and its vendored subset disappear (V8) — with them goes the product's last font dependency, and the ten-glyph gap the delivered System was carrying without seeing it: six glyphs were shipped without being drawn anywhere (error, link_off, menu, person_add, system_update_alt, volunteer_activism) and four were drawn without being used. Here everything is drawn, and the generator checks it: it refuses to produce this document if the survey and the catalog diverge by even one glyph, in either direction. A18 is no longer a promise, it is an assertion.

The complete set, at use size (16 px) — nothing is enlarged

direct — plain name, surface background: the grammar suffices, no trade-off (44) trade-off — name underlined with dots: a curve, a diagonal, a reduction had to be decided (27) hard — tile background: the grammar does not carry it at 16 px; drawn anyway, it is a deferral (14) reserved — dark: in the subset, used nowhere (4)

Gap measured against the grammar: 24 glyphs out of 78 use at least one arc, whereas the icon document uses one only in Wind's flap. The 14 hard ones are: account_balance, eco, favorite, flight, format_list_numbered, group_add, keyboard, person_add, pets, schedule_send, school, sports_esports, star, volunteer_activism. Twelve of them are the account markers — rendered at 12 px in the Settings swatch (the only pill use since A82) and at a 14-16 px outline in the row and the nav. At 12 px they drop below tier 16 itself, and they would need a fourth tier the document does not have. That is the price of the decision to keep the glyph in the swatch (V5); A82 raised the other uses to 14-16 px.

The tier — the real cost is not the drawing

A 2-unit stroke on a 24 grid, rendered at P px, measures 2 ÷ 24 × P. Wind's use sizes reach only one tier: no icon in the product goes up to 21 px. Everything falls into tier 16, snapped by hand, rectangle by rectangle — and the master does not follow scale: only 37% of its coordinates survive the 24 → 16 pass (you have to be a multiple of 3 to land exactly). This tier is not drawn; the glyphs below are the reduced masters, and they honestly show what that gives.

An open question, and it is not one of drawing. These 91 glyphs are redrawn from the shapes of Material Symbols — that is not the same thing as redistributing the font (Apache 2.0), and it is not a from-scratch creation either. The "About" line of the product says today "embedded font, Apache 2.0 license"; it will have to say something else, and exactly what remains to be decided before any adoption. Recorded, not swept aside.

The first launch is a four-step journey (A75), in a column centered on the app background, widened to 760 px on steps 2-4. Each step says, in this order: its title, the "Step n/4" line, its text, its content, then the march (Back / Continue, Finish at the end) — and Continue is never shown greyed out: absent as long as it cannot continue. A simple door: the domain chooses the flow. Gmail and Microsoft go to browser consent; any other domain reveals the server fields, pre-filled with imap.domain / smtp.domain, ports 993 / 465. The desk's three answers: note, waiting, error

Authorization in progress in your browser… Checking the connection to the server… Could not connect: the server did not respond.

Only one answer at a time, never a stack. Waiting is a muted note — accompanied since V2 by the ring, which replaces the stroke; the error is alert text under the form, never an overlay. This card's geometry is that of Settings: 40 px, 13 px entries, no shadow — one implementation, two surfaces (A11).

Display modes, and the handles

Three panes — the default 248 / 400 / 1fr. Two handles: nav↔list and list↔thread.
Two panes 248 / 1fr. The list takes the width, row template unchanged; opening a message is screen 03, full screen. One handle only.
One pane The list alone, without a right hairline; the nav lives in a drawer. No handle.

Widths are adjusted with the mouse (A44): a 7 px handle straddling each boundary, col-resize cursor, 2 px accent stroke on hover, on drag and on focus. Bounds: nav 180–400 px (default 248), list 300–640 px (default 400); the thread takes the rest. Double-click: return to default. On the keyboard (A8), the handle is a focusable separator: left/right arrows, 16 px per step. Widths are persisted; a value out of bounds → default. The window ceiling holds over the bounds: a boundary never crushes the thread below 120 px of reserve, and as the window shrinks, the list yields. Read marking, shortcuts, and the status bar are identical in every mode.

The list under refresh, and the gesture and its destination

Copy still syncing: try again in a moment.

A refresh shows no waiting state on rows already served: the displayed rows stay in place, each page is replaced when its fresh version arrives, without a skeleton and without a scroll jump (A23). The total does not fall back to zero. Delete, archive, send: the destination shows the message immediately, offline included (A24) — a local echo, visually identical, that the real copy replaces without visible movement. Other gestures on the echo wait for reconciliation, and the toast above says so — surface, hairline, sharp corner, single elevation, never more than one at a time. If the copy does not appear after a clean sync, the echo withdraws and the incident is logged.

Status bar and synchronization

The 36 px status bar is the region of the continuous: a single message at a time, dimmed 12 px text, no stacking. The timestamp re-renders every 30 seconds. The sync button (S-D1, A16), 26 px, lives on the right: "Sync" at rest, inhibited during a cycle, "Retry" on failure; its glyph stays still. Offline, the manual gesture always forces a sync. On the left lives the signature: since V2, the solid, still disc at rest, the hollow, spinning ring as soon as an action is in progress — cycle, full sync, catch-up, waiting to send. The percentage, when an exact denominator exists, lives in the row's text, never in the signature (A52 holds: the old stroke hidden at a partial length used to stay frozen on Chromium). Alert states are preceded by a 7 px dot.

1 · Up to date

… reading pane …
All messages are up to date · last synced 2 minutes ago Sync

2 · Cycle in progress — the ring spins, the % in the text

… reading pane …
Syncing · 2/4 · marie@atelier-brindille.fr · [Gmail]/All messages… · 37 % Syncing…

The current cycle is visible: account, position, folder or step, and percentage of the whole when one exists. Second-by-second polling during the cycle only.

3 · Total failure

… reading pane …
Sync failed · will retry automatically · last synced 12 minutes ago Try again

4 · Partial failure

… reading pane …
1 account of 2 unreachable · will retry automatically Try again

An unreachable account stays flagged even when the other one responds: without this state, the timestamp freshened by the reachable account would mask the anomaly.

5 · Offline

… reading pane …
Offline · last synced 18 minutes ago Sync

Network status comes from the OS via the WebView, instantly, with no timeout wait. The application serves the local store. Automatic cycles suspend; the return of the network triggers an immediate light pass. "Offline" is a state, not an incident: it lives in the row, never in the notice slot.

6 · Catch-up

… reading pane …
Catching up on messages · 412 to go · 88 % Syncing…

Catch-ups go through the same row (A55) — the percentage lives in the TEXT, capped at 99 while a body still remains to fetch, never "100 %" on a still-running tail. "Catching up on previews…" follows the same form.

7 · Capped search (A50)

… reading pane …
Search · 100 of 348 results Sync

Rendering is capped at 100: the total M says what the cap hides, without which the user would believe they had seen everything.

8 · Waiting to send

… reading pane …
2 messages waiting to send Syncing…

The outbox wait lives here, in the progress row; only failure escalates to a notice (see "Notices and progress").

Screen 03

Reading a conversation

Screen 03 is flat (A72): no more solid card — a reading column centered, capped at 960 px, the scene scrolls in a single flow. The reading pane and screen 03 are two frames of the same object (Thread component, shared state): enlarging reloads nothing, unfolding and body survive. The title moves to the display register (24 px, weight 340). Since A80 (D5), every card — unfolded as well as collapsed — carries the mailbox chip behind the sender's name, in normal weight: the name keeps authority. The account reads on the message; when every message in a thread comes from the same mailbox, the mention repeats — it is meant for the first glance. Under the same conditions as the list (field verdict of 2026-08-25): where the row stays silent — single-account view, single-account setup — the card stays silent too.

An attachment's veil (A70) — full coverage

Contrat_Vantis_v4.pdf1.2 MB at rest → Contrat_Vantis_v4.pdf1.2 MB Save

On hover as on focus, a veil fully covers the chip and states the action before the click: --sel background, internal accent border, download glyph, label "Save". The geometry does not move: the veil takes exactly the chip's box, nothing shifts, nothing is added to the row. It is never one more chip — one more chip would displace its neighbours and make the thread header's count a lie.

Transmission rules (A1, A61)

The message body sits 16 px from its card's edge, like the header. Converted plain text reads in a 68-character column; a sender's own layout is not constrained. The body always displays on a light slate — mail-render bakes ink #222222, background #ffffff (Palette::default) — regardless of theme: an email is composed for a light background, so it is shown as such. These are the only two values Wind sets in the document; a link keeps whatever the message, or the browser, gives it. The document's color-scheme follows the baked background: consistent scrollbar handles. The remote-image guard is per message (link_off glyph), attached to the body it concerns, on the application background — it is one of the two uses of --panel that V3 falls back to --bg.

The invitation card (A76) — a card WITHIN the message card

Invitation received, no reply

Invitation You have not replied
Sept.11
September workshop — scoping Thursday, September 11, 14:00 – 15:30 Milan Room · organised by Sofia Nardi
Accept Tentative Decline

It lives at the head of the content, before the files: it is the message's subject. Date tile in the --tile / --tileInk pair — the floor of Wind's objects, sharp corner, 1 px hairline, like the initials tile. Three neutral buttons (A14 intact: the card does not rank the reply); colour is carried by the icon, accent / neutral / alert, and the text always doubles it (A8). Sharp corner, no elevation: it belongs to the flow of the content, not to the thread.

Reply in place, and invitation cancelled

Invitation You accepted

Accept Tentative Decline
Invitation cancelled

The current reply is said via aria-pressed — --sel background, accent border, weight: A75's selection, the same everywhere. Cancellation turns the eyebrow to alert, the tile to dimmed (application background, muted ink) and the title strikethrough; the three buttons disappear — one does not reply to what no longer takes place. A floating hour shows as-is, never converted, and says so: "organiser's local time".

The thread's draft, in last position

A draft linked to the thread occupies the last position, as a collapsed message with a dashed accent stroke, with the mention ✎ Draft (alert, edit_note glyph) in place of the author and the last-edited time. Clicking anywhere on the block resumes the draft; the button names the gesture. The composer overlays it, the conversation stays mounted underneath. This block keeps the conversation consistent with the list, whose preview carries "Draft: ".

Reply is PER message (A58)

Since A58, Reply / Reply all / Forward target each message — a bar at the bottom of each unfolded card, ours included: replying on one's own message then targets the original recipients (the To for Reply, To+Cc for Reply all), never oneself. "Reply all" stays between Reply and Forward (A14). The thread's bar keeps only sorting gestures: Archive, Delete, Report as spam — which becomes "Not spam" (inbox glyph) in the Junk view — and, in Inbox only, "Pin" / "Unpin" (A73). Never a "More" menu.

The cap (25 Mo per message) is refused at the gesture, never at send: the chip doesn't appear, the alert message under the row names the refused file and the remaining space. Forwarding: three states per attachment, send held back

Annexe_tarifs.xlsx · retrieving… Contrat_Vantis_v4.pdf1,2 Mo Photos_reunion.zip · Try again

Each original attachment is retrieved from the server on open and added to the draft. Three states: retrieving (glyph hourglass_empty, dimmed), arrived (solid chip, removable), failed (name in alert color, “Try again” and a remove cross). Send stays held back as long as attachments are missing. On reply, no chip is inherited: mail convention doesn't carry over the original attachments.

The destructive confirmation (A57)

Delete this draft? This cannot be undone. Delete Cancel

“Delete draft” is the deliberate destructive gesture, on the right of the footer, in alert color. It appears only if there is something to discard, and it goes through a confirmation: the footer gives way to the question before the irreversible act. It is not to be confused with “Cancel”, which, itself, keeps — “Close = keep” covers the attachments.

The “From” line (A10, A78)

It is chosen when several accounts exist — native selector dressed in the tokens of the line; with a single account, it stays static text. Since A78, the selector reads “Name — address” when the account carries a custom name: the value stays the address, the functional sending data doesn't change, and the name never touches the From: of outgoing messages.

Startup screen

Migration

The migration modal is the only surface that is exclusive and blocking. It precedes the one-time updates that would freeze the interface if they ran on first launch: adopting a legacy database and rebuilding the search index. Its label is generic — true of both passes and their combination. The geometry is that of screen 01 (520 px column on the app background).

1 · Preparation — indeterminate gauge, never “0%”

Wind

Updating your mailbox.

Preparing…

Cancel

2 · In progress — the real count, and the percentage in the text

Wind

Updating your mailbox.

About 12,480 messages are being updated. This update only happens once and deletes nothing.

62% Cancel

3 · Failure — announced without loss, and resumable

Wind

Updating your mailbox.

The update was interrupted. Nothing is lost: it can be run again.

ResumeLater

The 6 px gauge stays indeterminate during preparation, never “0%”: a zero that doesn't move reads as stuck. “Cancel” interrupts the pass at its next checkpoint and undoes everything; it replays at the next launch, or immediately via “Resume”. The gauge stays a gauge and not the ring: it has an exact denominator, and A52 holds here as elsewhere — a percentage is stated in digits and in length, the signature never carries the measurement. With prefers-reduced-motion, the indeterminate gauge stops sliding and shows full, dimmed.

↑ Top of document

Notices and progress

The application's messages — updates, incidents, waits — obey the same rule as the rest: three regions, never a stack (A4).

1 · The notice slot, at the top — at most ONE, by fixed priority

Priority 1 — send failure

The message "Re: Relecture du contrat Vantis" was rejected by the server. Try again

The only notice that the outbox raises: the wait stays in the progress line, only the failure becomes a notice.

Priority 2 — update ready

Wind 0.8.1 is ready to be installed. Install

It never installs itself during a session: the notice proposes, the restart disposes.

Priority 3 — incident report

An incident has been logged. You can send it to the team. Send

The incident is already logged locally by the time the notice appears; sending it is a separate, optional gesture.

Priority 4 — telemetry consent

Allow sending anonymous usage statistics? AllowDecline

The last in the queue, and the only one without a close cross: a consent gets answered, it never gets dismissed.

At most one persistent notice at a time, chosen by this fixed priority. The notice is a light surface with the sole elevation. The next one appears only once the previous is resolved or dismissed. The "drafts" source has been removed: resuming a draft lives in the Drafts folder and in the conversation, never in the slot.

2 · The progress line, at the bottom

Syncing · 2/4 · marie@atelier-brindille.fr · 37 % Syncing…

At most one progress line (sync or catch-up), in muted text, below the notice in priority. The outbox wait ("N waiting") lives here. The signature on the left, the sync button on the right. The line stays unique.

3 · The toast, and the blocking surfaces

Account added.

The toast states a fait accompli and fades away on its own: surface, hairline, sharp corner, single elevation, never more than one, never an irreversible action. At startup, only two surfaces occupy the screen, in this order: the migration modal (exclusive and blocking) then, on first launch, the onboarding flow — it covers the window but blocks no machine: synchronization starts behind it. Outside these two, nothing ever blocks. And nothing touches the database before migration (A41).

States

Message row

Two templates — bare h1 and h2 carrying its chip row (A44) — both probed by the windowing mechanics, and adjustable since A83: the row's vertical air has three notches ("Low" 88 px, "Medium" 100, "High" 112; the chip row adds 27 px in every case). The probes stay permanently mounted to re-measure themselves — a height frozen on the old notch would make the scrollbar lie. A row that has something to say carries a 24 px chip row and grows with it; there is no reserved row on bare rows. Since A81 the row no longer has a lead column (the initials tile has left the list): the header row carries, in order, the unread disk, the sender's name, the mailbox block (A80 — in unified inbox and in search) and the time; the subject and preview follow, full width. Below, a unified-inbox mockup: "Travail" is an account with a personalized name and a marker; the other account has neither — its mailbox still speaks, through the address (D8).

Read, at restUnread (account with no marker, D8)Hover Selected (carrying row)Pinned

Transmission rules. The unread state is told by the 9 px disk and by the weight — never by a filled dot, never by a subject color; the mailbox block, itself, stays at normal weight on an unread row (A8/V6: weight carries what the row SAYS, not its circumstances). The mailbox block (A80): in in muted ink, the marker's stroke at the account's hue (14 px, absent if the account has no marker — D8), the label — personalized name (A78) or address; tooltip "label — address". Three truncation rules, each in one sentence: the time never gets cut (it is the column's reading landmark); the block yields three times faster than the sender and never takes more than a third of the row (measured ceiling, PLAN-REPERE-LIGNE §1.3); both end in an ellipsis, never a hard cut. In the Sent folder (A48), the sender being SELF, the row states the recipient — "To: …" — drawn from the stored To of the ENVELOPE; a send not yet caught up falls back on the sender, never a mute row. The chip row is factual and silent: it never carries a state or an alert — counting, not signaling. Hover tints the background without shifting the content. Selection takes --sel and the 2 px accent stripe at the left edge; never a shadow nor a white surface. The pinned row takes the --tile ground and the keep mark (A73) — and on this ground, the accent only serves as a stripe, never as a label (measured: 4.38:1). On the e or Del shortcut, the row below becomes the selection (A38): in three panes it opens its pane as on click, in two or one pane it only lights up. The mouse gesture does not shift the selection. Chips follow the same rules as the Thread head: "n messages" if the thread has more than one, "n files" if there are attachments — 0 as long as the body hasn't been fetched, the chip appears as catch-up proceeds, never wrongly. In search, a result is a message and not a conversation: the thread chip does not appear there, by construction.

Amendments journal

This journal is an archive of dated facts: it does not get rewritten. The seventy-eight amendments A1–A78 are reproduced verbatim from the previous System (docs/archives/systeme.v1.dc.html) — rereading them is the only way to know what the Elements direction overturns and what it keeps. The adoption decisions are recorded at the top, under the reference V-n — series closed at V14 (PLAN-ELEMENTS, CE decision D1 of 2026-08-24): since the adoption, amendments resume the A-n series, following on from A78.

The v2 decisions — 14 entries

DateRef.Decision
2026-08-24V1The brand becomes the Elements icon, and teal enters the token table. The envelope on a tile with a half-disk flap replaces the envelope with the "W" dot; the dot disappears — the set never puts anything inside a cornered container, and the "W" was just restating the name. The two brand colors stay frozen (W-D3): tile #F2EDE3, teal #1F8A8A. Teal enters the table under the new token --brand, measured COMPONENT (3:1) and never text, and it is doubled with an ink --accent #1A7A7A of the same hue for everything that is read.
2026-08-24V2The hitofude stroke dies; the disk/ring pair replaces it. Chief Engineer decision. A28, A36 and A40 fall — the calligraphic signature has no place in a fully constructed system. The solid --brand disk of 9 px tells rest, the hollow ring of the same diameter tells that an action is spinning: it is not one more shape, it is the same disk with a 2 px wall and its upper quarter open. Two locations, the status bar and the migration modal. A52 holds and is reinforced: the percentage lives in the TEXT, never in the signature. This is an accepted loss — the stroke had cost several projects, including the A40 discovery (SMIL in the mask). Pitted against six other proposals on 2026-08-24, and confirmed. At the Chief Engineer's request, seven signatures were drawn and animated at real size in a real status bar (spikes/direction-elements/v2/signatures.mjs). Verdict: the ring is kept. What was set aside, and for what reason — so that nothing gets re-proposed without a new reason: the disk's pulse freezes on the resting state (A8 broken); the sweep reads as a measurement (A52 broken) and resurrects the thin bar removed by A36; the square with an eighth-turn and the four corners put a container where V4/V14 reserve the round to state — and the square overshoots by 1.86 px on each side while turning (9 × √2 = 12.73); the brand's flap takes away its orientation from the set's only oriented shape. Only alternating solid ↔ hollow held the four rules like the ring: it was set aside on sight, a flicker reading as "alert". The ring remains the only one of the seven that adds no shape, no color, no value.
2026-08-24V3--panel dies: two grounds instead of three. Chief Engineer decision. Navigation, header, banners and status bar stop being recessed; the 1 px hairline alone carries the separation. Wind stays flat — A29, A30, A46 and A72 all hold: the 18-radius bordered panels of the icon document are NOT carried over. The token count doesn't move: --panel goes out, --brand comes in, seventeen roles. Cost noted: 16 uses of var(--panel) in 7 components, of which two are not panel backgrounds but states — the dimmed date tile of a cancelled invitation and the background of the image guard: they fall back on --bg. Side effect: the hairline, which A28 declared decorative, becomes load-bearing — this document measures it, threshold = the hairline shipped.
2026-08-24V4The round is returned to the disk. Chief Engineer decision. The disk has only one use left in the whole system: to tell state. Two rounds are therefore removed — the initials avatar becomes a square tile (28 px, radius 2 — brought to 0 by V14, ground --tile, ink --tileInk, 1 px hairline: measured, the tile is only 1.04:1 on the light background, without the hairline it doesn't exist), and the navigation's solid unread dot becomes a number in tabular figures at the accent. In exchange, an unread row's unread state gains a 9 px disk. What is overturned, exactly: A29 point 2, which IMPOSED the solid unread dot in the nav; and the prose rule "never by a colored dot" from the Message row section, which carried no reference. A29 aimed at a dot that shouted; the disk doesn't shout, it is the same object as the status bar ring, and it is placed on the row's geometric center by construction. The sender's and subject's weight remains: unread is never told by color alone (A8).
2026-08-24V5The account marker KEEPS its glyph. Chief Engineer decision, against the icon document's doctrine, which never puts anything inside a disk. The deciding fact is measured: none of the six element hues carries a glyph at 4.5:1 in both polarities, and A74 puts a glyph in the dot PRECISELY so the account isn't told by color alone (A8, WCAG 1.4.1). Applying the direction to the letter would regress accessibility. The swatch runs through .rep[data-teinte] and follows polarity: a hue frozen for light would render its glyph at 2.35:1 at night — this document's first draft made exactly that mistake in its own mockups, it is corrected. Cost kept and logged: twelve glyphs rendered at 10-12 px, hence below the 16 tier itself (see V9).
2026-08-24V6One display register, weight 340. The conversation title (24 px) and the home hero (40 px) move to weight 340, letter-spacing -.03em — the icon document's grammar. The principle doesn't move: authority stays graded by SIZE, and nothing below 24 px changes. Explicit fallback: without a variable font, 340 falls back to 400 — the title remains a title, it is never bold, and no drawing depends on the weight.
2026-08-24V7Two themes, and only two — overturns A42. The fourteen Wada combinations and their fourteen nights are removed; "Elements" (default, no attribute) and "Elements · night" remain. The token table goes from 476 cells to 34, onboarding step 3 from 28 cards to 2, the Settings Themes group likewise. What is lost: choice. What is gained: two truly composed and measured polarities, instead of twenty-eight to maintain. Adoption cost noted file by file in the Themes section: seven files, and three gate checks to revisit — not just the NOMBRE_ATTENDU floor, as this document's first draft wrongly claimed.
2026-08-24V8The glyphs are drawn, the font dies. The 78 glyphs of the inventory are redrawn in the document's grammar and served as inline SVG. Material Symbols Rounded and its vendored subset disappear, and with them the CDN link that this document was still pulling while the application forbids itself from doing so. Side effect: the ten glyphs gap closes. Six glyphs were shipped without being drawn anywhere (error, link_off, menu, person_add, system_update_alt, volunteer_activism) and four were drawn without being used — A18 was no longer true on ten glyphs. The Icons section's listing IS now the inventory, and the generator refuses to produce this document if the listing and the catalogue diverge by a single glyph, in either direction: A18 becomes an assertion. Three merges remain to be arbitrated. And one question that isn't about drawing: the 78 glyphs are redrawn after the Material shapes — the "About" line that says "embedded font, Apache 2.0 license" must change, and the attribution wording remains to be settled before any adoption.
2026-08-24V9Open debt: the 16 tier is not drawn. The icon document imposes three tiers; Wind's usage sizes only reach one — no product icon rises to 21 px. Everything falls into the 16 tier, which snaps by hand, rectangle by rectangle, and the master doesn't scale into it: only 37% of its coordinates survive the 24 → 16 pass, the remaining 63% land on thirds of a pixel. The twelve account markers, rendered at 10-12 px, fall below the 16 tier itself. Costing: 74 masters done, 74 16-tiers to do, 12 10-12 tiers to invent — 160 drawings total, 46% done. This document shows the reduced masters: it doesn't claim the tier exists.
2026-08-24V10Three radii, two shapes, and one platform metric — intermediate step, superseded the same day by V14. 10 px for surfaces, 6 px for controls, plus 2 px for the tile: a tile is neither a surface nor a control, and at 28 px a radius of 6 makes it frankly round, it would take back from the disk the uniqueness V4 just gave it. The rule holds for this document as for the product — the first draft used eight other values in its own illustrations, they were brought back to the three. The pill and the disk are declared shapes, not radii; the application icon's radius (15/64) is a platform metric, outside the system. Accepted side effect: the navigation row goes from radius 8 (A29) to radius 6 — the system has no 8. What remains of V10: the three shape tokens, the "pill and disk are not radii" doctrine, and the platform exception. What falls: the values 10 / 6 / 2, zeroed out by V14 — V4's argument, applied halfway here, is taken all the way there.
2026-08-24V11The brand has two regimes, and the document says which applies where. In tile form — application icon, onboarding, migration, "About" — it is frozen outside themes (W-D3): structure #141414, tile #F2EDE3, teal #1F8A8A, identical in both polarities. In glyph form — header, drawer — it follows the current ink and --brand. This is not a breach of W-D3 but its boundary: the tile carries its own ground, a bare glyph has none, and a frozen #141414 placed on the night background would be invisible (1.25:1). The first draft applied both regimes without stating them.
2026-08-24V12Defect found in the delivered document — and repaired. The amendments journal row carrying A48 had only two cells: its date cell was missing, and the reference occupied the date column. This was invisible on render — the table closes on its own — but any automated reader of the journal tripped over it. Fixed in docs/design/system.dc.html on 2026-08-24, on the Chief Engineer's verdict: a cell added, dated 2026-08-16 from the amendment's content ("verdicts D1-D4 of 2026-08-16") and in the exact format of its neighbors. One row added, nothing else touched; the coherence gate stays green. The journal's 78 rows now all have their three cells, and this document has nothing more to restore.
2026-08-24V13Review of v2 by its author, and what it corrected. The document was reread against its own statements, backed by measurements and greps. Eleven contradictions found and fixed, three of which matter: (1) the marker dot was frozen for light in the mockups — glyph at 2.35:1 and dot at 2.62:1 at night, exactly the accessibility regression that V5 claims to avoid (fixed by .rep[data-teinte]); (2) the adoption cost was underestimated — "only NOMBRE_ATTENDU" was false, it's seven files and three gate checks (listed in writing in the Themes section); (3) the email body slab invented its values — #1a1a1a and an imaginary link #1a5f7a, when mail-render bakes #222222 on #ffffff and sets no link color. Added along the way: the attachment veil as absolute overlay and not as one more chip (A70), the invitation card (A76) and search (A50), which neither this document nor the shipped one drew, the three migration states, the four fixed-priority notices, the seven Settings groups, the composer's color picker and deadline card, the layout diagrams, pinned items at the top of the list, the toast, the list-footer counter, and the :focus-visible rule that the document stated without applying to itself.
2026-08-24V14Corners go SQUARE. Zero radius. Chief Engineer's verdict, on a question he raised — "to be consistent with the art direction, shouldn't we move to square-cornered shapes?" What measurement established: the 78 glyphs, 219 sub-paths and 654 drawing commands use no rounded corner (miter and butt everywhere); but the two documents presenting them use eight different radii — 18, 16, 14, 12, 11, 10, 9, 2, plus the pill. The direction thus has a strict grammar for what it DRAWS and none for what it CONTAINS: it couldn't be copied, it had to be decided. What decided it: V4's argument — "the round tells state" — cannot bear being applied halfway. A card at 10, a button at 6 and a tile at 2 are three degrees of roundness that say nothing and dilute the one round that speaks. The rule becomes shorter than the one it replaces: zero radius; two round shapes, and they say something — the disk (state, identity) and the switch's pill (the slide). It is V3's move: kill one token to let another carry the meaning. What moves, exactly: surfaces, controls, tiles, cards, modals, chips, fields, tabs, nav rows, application window, invitation, toast, notice, color picker — all to 0. The gauge loses its pill along the way: a progress bar is not a load-bearing shape, it is a container. This document's theme toggle, which is a segmented control and not a pill, follows the rule too. What doesn't move: the disk, the ring, the marker dot and the switch handle (50%), the switch track (999). The exception, declared and permanent: the application icon keeps its platform radius (15/64) — the OS dictates it. It becomes the only rounded shape in the whole product, and it is visible at the most-looked-at spot: logged, not swept under the rug. The cost, and its verdict. The only serious argument against was the platform idiom: Windows 11 rounds everything, and a sharp-cornered application could read as foreign there. It did not get judged on a mockup. Field finding of 2026-08-24: the document rendered in the Chief Engineer's own browser, browsed on the real screen — square corners validated, kept. Reservation named, because a finding is worth what its medium carries: what was looked at was the document, not an application window set next to Explorer and Windows Settings. The Fluent idiom will be re-checked at the first shipped window; if it says something else, the return still fits in one line — put 10 / 6 / 2 back into the three tokens of socle.mjs. That is precisely why they exist, and they stay. What was removed: the "Corners" toggle that served for the arbitration. A System that offers two states of its own rule is a System that hasn't decided — the comparison remains, in the "The corners" section, as a trace of what was set aside and why.

2026-08-15 A39The window never freezes, CE field finding (PLAN-GELS): at startup, the window stayed unresponsive for several seconds — no click, no move. Root cause: in Tauri 2, a command declared without async runs on the main thread, the message pump's thread; every synchronous command that opened the database froze the window for its whole duration (measured: 25.2 s of cumulative freezes over 40 s, worst freeze 4.6 s — preview catch-up in batches of 2,000). Rule: every command that opens the database, touches a file, or the vault is async — the pump only pumps; only pure state commands (atomic, detached) stay synchronous, named and justified. The preview catch-up batch goes from 2,000 to 500 (short write lock, UI gestures don't hit BUSY). Held by a gate (main-thread-guard.mjs) and a budget: no pump freeze > 150 ms (freeze-probe.py) — re-measured after the remedy: zero freeze over 40 s, same decor.
2026-08-15 A40The hitofude stroke lives during cycles, CE field finding (PLAN-GELS validation): "the stroke stays fixed during a sync." Two roots, measured on a copy of the real database. 1. Progress was freezing at 99% after any triage: the gesture removes the local row immediately (echo, E3) but remote_total dates from the last SELECT — 5 archives + 1 deletion waiting for replay were enough to hold sync_percent under 100 ("never 100 until finished"), and the stroke switched to "full at the percentage" mode, still, on every cycle. Rule: departures awaiting replay (archive, delete, move) no longer count in the denominator; markings don't touch it; capped at zero per mailbox. 2. The vague loop was stillborn: the animated path lives in the SVG <mask>, an unrendered subtree where Chromium doesn't run CSS animations (playState idle, proven on the real window). The path switches to SMIL (<animate>, 115→0 over 2 s then full, 4 s loop); the fade stays in CSS on the rendered path; prefers-reduced-motion (A8) held by hand — SMIL doesn't obey the global CSS block, the <animate> isn't rendered when motion is reduced, the stroke falls back full and still. The hitofudeDraw keyframes leave system.css (dead); hitofudeFade remains. Proof: dashoffset movement measured over CDP during a real cycle; an e2e test holds the presence of the <animate> in the status bar's stroke.
2026-08-15 A41Nothing touches the database before the migration modal, review finding of 2026-08-15 (window-freeze project): language restoration, played before the first render, opened the database (lang_get, and lang_set on first launch) — on a legacy database, adoption was paid for silently when the language loaded, with no modal, no progress, no cancellation, against ADR 0012. Rule: reading the language is a read-only probe (the pending_adoption pattern: missing file or missing table, no trace, no migration), and the language detected at first launch gets set after the modal, only if the migration probe has answered. A read failure is not an absent preference: it counts as a session fallback, never a write. The modal stays the first surface to pay for adoption — visible, interruptible.

2026-08-17 A50Search — the cap tells the truth (PLAN-RECHERCHE, deferred item settled, CE decisions of 2026-08-17). Search renders at most 100 rows (was 50). When this cap bites, the status bar says "Search · 100 of N results" (statut.recherchePlafond) instead of letting one believe there are exactly 100: the EXACT number comes from a COUNT on the index, computed only if the render is capped (a search that renders fewer already knows its total; the COUNT measured at 3.5 ms, negligible). The cap is 100, but the real budget lever lies elsewhere, revealed in the field: on a very common 3-character prefix (36k matches), the BM25 floor (~80 ms, and it rises with the corpus) exceeds the budget regardless of the cap. The ADR 0004 date-sort valve is therefore armed: beyond WIDE_QUERY_THRESHOLD (10,000 matches), search_capped sorts by DATE instead of BM25 — the budget holds (~66 ms on "fac"), and for such a wide query, date is a better order anyway than a "relevance ranking" of a 3-letter stub. Below the threshold, BM25 as before. "Unlimited" stays declined: it would hit the SELECT_UNIFIED per-row hydration and the unwindowed result list — a true "see everything" would need a virtualized list + cursor pagination (known debt).
2026-08-17 A51Search — "load more" (PLAN-CHARGER-PLUS, CE decisions of 2026-08-17). Below the results list, a discreet, centered "Show the next N results" button (liste.chargerPlus, N = min(100, remaining)) stacks the next batch — the list grows, the bar reads "200 of M", "300 of M"… The button disappears once everything is shown. Soft cap ~1000 rows (D1): the list not being windowed, past ten batches the button gives way to the prompt "Refine your search (from:, to:, date:)" (liste.affiner) rather than weighing down the DOM endlessly. Mechanism (calibrated in the field): a two-stage pagination — a bare OFFSET on the hydrated query degrades to O(offset) (SQLite hydrates the skipped rows), so stage 1 is ordered KEYS only (the OFFSET only skips light keys), stage 2 only hydrates the 100 of the page, reordered; flat cost at any depth. Since sort only depends on the total, slices chain with no gap nor duplicate. A new keystroke restarts from page 1 (anti-race token: an in-flight batch that has become stale is dropped). ink/surface button pair, ink/sel hover (contrast validated).

The send leaves as multipart/alternative (derived text + HTML), the Drafts mirror likewise; the Sent echo shows the composed HTML; a reply's quote becomes a blockquote with a left hairline.
