Two guards born from this project: the composer's pre-focus never steals a focus already set in the card; the editor is recognized as INPUT by the keyboard router (isContentEditable) — without which typing "c", "e" or Del in the body triggered the global shortcuts.
2026-08-20 A63Reconnect an account from Settings (2026-08-20 field finding, fixed the same day). An expired or revoked OAuth token (invalid_grant) left the user STRANDED: the notice slot said "Account not reconnected", but "Try again" replayed the silent connection — doomed with a dead token — and no gesture relaunched the consent flow. Now Settings > Accounts states each account's status: a row with a dead token carries link_off + "Disconnected" (alert hue — same glyph, same meaning as the reconnection notice in the slot, A8 respected) and a "Reconnect" button that replays the browser consent on the EXISTING row (nothing re-syncs, nothing is lost); the failure is stated BELOW the row and the gesture replays (the removal pattern). Identity guard: consent given for a DIFFERENT address is flatly refused — "reconnect X" never silently connects Y. A healthy account's row doesn't change. Immediate field finding (same day): the slot notice no longer offers "Try again" — the silent connection it replayed is doomed with a dead token — but "Settings", the direct door to the Accounts page and the repair gesture; "Dismiss" remains. No new glyph.
2026-08-20 A64The list only asks for what it shows, and the empty screen only asserts itself after proof (PLAN-DEFILEMENT-PROFOND, 2026-08-20 field finding). A held scrollbar drag in Archive triggered one page per position crossed (~161 list_category calls for 2 s of gesture, measured at the measure-scroll.mjs bench); the core's serialized queue (ADR 0019) drained over minutes on the real database — meanwhile, ".." blocks stuck in place and, worse, "No messages here." in EVERY folder: the source change reset total = 0 without invalidating the empty-state display guard, the screen asserted an emptiness it hadn't proven while page 0 waited behind the queue. Two rules now: (1) at most two pages in flight, and on every free flight the list serves the most useful page of the current window — never those of a position gone by; a drag keeps feeding the screen as the gesture proceeds, the core's queue doesn't grow (max simultaneous flights 1, end-to-end p50 wait 2,408 → 17 ms, rows served 0.5 s after the stop, immediate folder switch — page 0 of a source that hasn't answered even jumps AHEAD of the gauge, overflow bounded to one flight). Same-day field finding, three tightenings: a single flight (the core serializes — a second flight only added a stale page in front of the useful one); counts leave the display path — the page no longer carries a total (a full-corpus count, NOT EXISTS probe per row, ~240 ms on 200k+ cold, was paid on EVERY page, even page 0: Archive's first render at ~5 s in the field): the ROWS display first, a short page states its own exact end (small folders never pay for a count), category_total is only requested once the pump is idle and the scrollbar adjusts on its arrival; and the nav probe only pays for what the nav states (A29: unread alone) — nav_snapshot was recomputing eight per-account counters every 10 s, including the full-corpus total, the application's most expensive one, to display only two of them. (2) The empty state requires proof: as long as the current source hasn't answered, the screen shows the waiting skeleton ("…" rows) — "No messages here." only displays once a page from THIS source has come back with zero rows. The cost of a deep page outside the inbox stays O(offset) (~250 ms at offset 80,000, CE decision D1: accepted, only one in flight, logged as debt). No new glyph.
2026-08-21 A65The send echo tells the truth, the address autocompletes (PLAN-RETOURS-5, 2026-08-21 field finding; CE decisions D1-D5 of the same day). (1) Sent's temporary entry — the local echo that shows the send before the server copy arrives (PLAN-REACTIVITE E3) — displayed "To: envoyes" (its destination's slug served as recipient) and an "Attachments" title with nothing below. Now the echo carries its real recipients (copied from the send journal at its birth, to_addrs column — list and message head state them like any row) and its attachments as metadata (name + weight from the send journal, echo_attachments) as inert chips (D2): the bytes left with the send, nothing gets saved during the reconciliation window — the echo still dies when the real copy comes in (same message_id), this contract doesn't change. (2) Address autocompletion (D3-D4): under To, Cc and Bcc, a menu suggests from the correspondents directory — learned from mail seen (senders with their display name, junk and trash excluded; recipients of OUR sends), never an edited address book — on the current segment (after the last comma), from 2 characters, prefix matched on address, name, or a word of the name, ranked by recency + frequency, 8 at most. The suggestion shows "Name + address" (name at 600, address muted) but inserts the BARE address (D3 — the send path and its anti-injection guard don't change). Keyboard: ↓ ↑ choose, Enter inserts, Escape closes the menu without leaving the field; click likewise. Menu on the card's tokened surface (radius 8, standard shadow, hover --hover, choice --sel). A single query flight at a time, debounced at 150 ms (A64's lesson: never a burst in the serialized queue). No new glyph.
2026-08-21 A66The composer header carries the footer's background (PLAN-RETOURS-6, R4). CE report: the "New message" header should be the same color as Wind's footer. The footer (the status bar) is on --panel; the composer's formatting bar already was — the header adopts it: the card frames itself top/bottom in the same hue, the kicker stays --muted (a combination already in service in the status bar, contrasts held across the 28 themes). No new glyph.
2026-08-21 A67The composer's "Important" button (PLAN-RETOURS-6, R3; placement retouched in the 2026-08-21 field pass). A state toggle (priority_high glyph, aria-pressed; marked state = selection background + accent hue) living in the formatting bar, at its neighbors' exact format — icon alone, never a label (field verdict: the footer, reserved for actions, was getting crowded); the tooltip states the GESTURE: "Mark the message as important" (2nd field pass) — a MESSAGE state, not an action: it's saved with the draft (drafts.important column, resuming restores it, toggling it alone counts as a real edit), enters the send journal (outbox.important) and leaves as headers X-Priority: 1 + Importance: high — the pair that Outlook/Thunderbird set and that Gmail and others read; an ordinary send carries neither. Scope: the composer ALONE — displaying important received messages is a separate project (§2.6). 1 new glyph (58 → 59, see A69).
2026-08-21 A68The signature manager (PLAN-RETOURS-6, R1; CE decisions D3/D4 of 2026-08-21). Settings gains a Signature group (signature glyph): one block per account — a reduced rich editor (bold/italic/underline, D3; contenteditable + legacy execCommand, the output crosses THE ammonia boundary at save time, like any body), a scope toggle "Also in replies and forwards" (D4, a choice PER ACCOUNT, default: new messages only) and "Apply to all accounts" — which copies this account's SIGNATURE AND SCOPE to all the others, and it shows: their editors and toggles update on screen (2026-08-21 field finding). Storage: prefs (signature.<account>), no migration. In the composer: a new message carries the signature below two blank lines (cursor at the top); a reply/forward places it between the lead-in and the quote if the account's scope says so; changing the sending account reloads the new account's signature (2026-08-21 field finding, refined in the 2nd pass) — on any composition whose body hasn't been touched, replies and forwards included: the TEMPLATE posted at opening recomposes lead-in and quote identically, only the signature changes (and the new account's D4 scope decides); a typed keystroke takes priority, never overwritten; resuming a draft, with no template, never recomposes. Anti-churn guard: a body that Wind alone posted (signature, no keystroke) counts as empty — closing a blank composition never sows a phantom draft. No images in signatures (the allowlist doesn't move), no multi-signatures (§2.6). 1 new glyph (see A69).
2026-08-21 A69Deferred send (PLAN-RETOURS-6, R2; CE decisions D1/D2 of 2026-08-21). The composer footer gains "Send later" (schedule_send glyph): a card above the footer (color-picker idiom) — deadline preset at +1 h (native datetime-local), "Schedule" button, and the local semantics stated plainly (D1): "The message will leave at this time if Wind is open — otherwise at the next launch" (SMTP offers no server-side scheduling). Mechanics: the send is logged right away (golden rule) with its deadline (outbox.send_at_epoch); the drain — single gate — ignores a scheduled one not yet due; the toast states the deadline, never "sent"; the Sent echo is only born on departure. The status bar says "N scheduled send(s) · leaves {when}" (a dated rest, not a looping stroke — a scheduled send doesn't wait on the network), the notice slot carries the nearest one with "Cancel send" (D2): cancelling removes the journal entry and recreates the whole draft (recipients, body, marking, attachments with bytes) — reversible, nothing is lost; too late (already gone) is stated honestly. Departure: the send probe (10 s) arms a short timer (< 60 s of the deadline) — ~1 s precision, no long-lived timer that would outlive a cancellation. A67-A69 glyph tally: 3 new (priority_high, schedule_send, signature), subset 58 → 61, cache-buster ?v=61.
2026-08-21 A70Hovering an attachment STATES the action (PLAN-RETOURS-7, R1; CE decision D1 of 2026-08-21). On hover as on keyboard focus (A8), a veil covers the chip — same geometry, absolute overlay: the row never reflows — with the download glyph and the product's word: "Save" (D1: the click opens "Save as", the toast says "Attachment saved" — one single vocabulary, "download" doesn't enter it). Opaque --sel background (the existing ink/sel hover pair, contrasts held). Never on an echo's inert chip (no promise, RETOURS-5 D2) nor during an in-flight save. 1 new glyph (see A73).
2026-08-21 A71Attachments BEFORE the body (PLAN-RETOURS-7, R2). In an expanded message card, the "Attachments" section moves to right under the message head, before the image guard and the body — the eye finds them without scrolling through the mail; the image guard stays glued to the body it concerns. Same container, no new drawing; the order is guarded by e2e (no test locked it down before).
2026-08-21 A72Screen 03 flat (PLAN-RETOURS-7, R3; CE decision D2 of 2026-08-21 — overturns A46's "screen 03 keeps its full card"). The open conversation now takes the pane's exact shape: no enclosing elevation — each message in its own elevated card, the scene on --bg scrolls as a single flow (thread head with no hairline, action bar in the flow). Reading column centered, capped at 960 px (D2): the wide screen stays at reading width. Pane and screen 03 remain two frames of the same object (Thread component) — the shape is now ONE. e2e guard twin to the pane's flatness.
2026-08-21 A73Pin a conversation (PLAN-RETOURS-7, R4; CE decisions D3-D5 of 2026-08-21). "Pin"/"Unpin" (keep/keep_off glyphs, aria-pressed) joins the thread bar — the triage gestures' home (D3, never a gesture on rows) — in Inbox only (D4). A pinned conversation lives at the top of the list, in a section devoted to it in the flow (same rows, keep mark "Pinned" in the chip row), and leaves its date position (D5: never the same row twice); unpinning returns it there. Field finding (2026-08-21): the pinned row takes the current mailbox tile's drawing (nav, W2-D5) — --tile background, --tileInk ink — to stand out from the flow at first glance; the hue holds on hover, selection keeps its accent stripe. Local data (IMAP has no such concept; the \Flagged star is a different semantic, never repurposed), envelope key — it survives thread rebuilding and follows the whole thread (a reply that moves the head detaches nothing). Echoes, drafts and search: out of scope (§2.6). A70-A73 glyph tally: 3 new (download, keep, keep_off), subset 61 → 64, cache-buster ?v=64.
2026-08-22 A74The account marker (PLAN-RETOURS-8, R1; CE decisions D1-D3 of 2026-08-22). An account can carry a marker — an icon from a dedicated set + a hue from the marker swatch — chosen in Settings > Accounts (the row's icon is the door; a picker card under the row; a marker only exists whole). It replaces person in the nav (20 px dot, row and tile) and marks rows in unified inbox only (D3) with a 16 px badge under the avatar — the h1/h2 templates don't move. The swatch is a family of CONTENT colors (like the composer's color picker, never theme tokens), born of a measurement: no single hue holds 3:1 on the light backgrounds AND on the -night ones (worst case iris-nuit/sel) — each family thus lives in two variants (dark for the 14 light themes, white glyph; light for the 14 -night ones, ink #1c1b1b), served by [data-theme$="-nuit"] and measured by the contrast gate (≥ 3:1 component, glyph ≥ 4.5:1). The icon set is DEDICATED (D2): reserved for markers, never reused elsewhere — A3 held by reservation; work returns (removed in A32) to the sole meaning of marker. Local preference (prefs, signature pattern), default = neutral person: the update is invisible for the existing base. Glyph tally: 12 new, subset 64 → 76, cache-buster ?v=76. Along the way: the Settings groups count had said "six" since A68 — fixed ("seven", Signature listed).
2026-08-22 A75The first-launch flow (PLAN-RETOURS-8, R2; CE decision D4 of 2026-08-22 — amends "onboarding that only asks for one address" (Principles) and the migration modal's exclusivity ("nothing else ever blocks"); form settled in the field the same day, sixteen findings across three passes, fixed within the session). First launch becomes a four-step flow in screen 01's geometry, each step saying title → "Step n/4" → text, and Continue never grayed out — absent while it can't proceed: 1. accounts — "Welcome to Wind" (hitofude behind the brand), 40 px address bar with "Add" button (PRIMARY while Continue is absent — no account: it's THE gesture —, secondary afterward), no "server detected" note, bar collapsed behind "Add another email address" from the first address on; the revealed generic counter HIDES Continue, its own "Add" is always primary, "Back" collapses the fields (A11's counter unchanged under this new skin; no account, no Continue — D4); 2. layout — ONE real capture of the app (Clarity mockup, e2e/capture-onboarding.mjs, cropped above the status bar) that follows the hovered/focused button and settles on the choice, three buttons centered below, the whole in ONE elevation; 3. theme — 28 miniature windows in FICHES colors, drawn in the CHOSEN layout; 4. summary — "Check your choices before continuing.", the three choices ("Accounts", "Layout", "Theme") in SIDE-BY-SIDE door-cards with MINIATURES under the text (layout capture, theme window), "Return to this step" veil on hover/focus (A70's rules, arrow_back glyph), click returns to the step, then Finish. Card and button selection = --sel background + thickened accent outline (inner stripe). Choices apply and persist instantly — the theme gesture, zero backend cost. wind-accueil-fait / wind-accueil-commence marks (localStorage, V-D4): an existing installation is deemed onboarded, a STARTED then abandoned flow resumes, a machine back to zero accounts finds the counter alone. The A41 order holds: migration, language, onboarding — the flow covers the window but blocks no machine (sync starts behind it). Debt D-10 (onMount order with no e2e assertion) reopened as expected (this project touches onMount): the order is verified on the record — the onboarding decision lives in chargerNav, AFTER assurer() and language setting — but the `prefs.lang` assertion is still to be written (D-10 stays open).
2026-08-22 A76The meeting invitation card (PLAN-INVITATIONS; CE decisions D1-D7 of 2026-08-22). A message carrying an iTIP invitation (text/calendar) shows it as a card AT THE HEAD of the content of the expanded card — before attachments and body: it is the message's whole point. The card (10 px surface radius, no elevation — it belongs to the content flow) states: kicker "Invitation" ("Invitation cancelled" in --alert for a CANCEL; "Reply to your invitation" for a received REPLY), status on the right ("You haven't responded" / "You accepted/declined/tentatively responded" — D6: Wind's last SENT reply is authoritative), a date tile (abbreviated month + day number, the current-mailbox tile's --tile/--tileInk pair; dimmed in --panel/--muted for a CANCEL), the title (struck through for a CANCEL), the time in the machine's local timezone, location · organizer. An hour in an UNRESOLVED timezone displays as is, suffixed "organizer's local time" (D1 guard) — never a misleading conversion. Three NEUTRAL buttons "Accept / Tentative / Decline" (D4: no accent — A14 stays intact, the card doesn't rank the reply), at the message-action template (30 px); the current reply is told by aria-pressed — --sel background + accent stripe, A75's selection; replying stays possible after a reply (D6, new iTIP email). The reply leaves through THE outbox (journal first; offline: at next launch, A69's stated semantics), subject in the product's language ("Accepted: {title}", D5). D3: the inline calendar part is NOT a file — never again a phantom "piece-jointe.calendar" chip — filtered at the source for new scans, and existing data is RE-SCANNED once (pieces-calendrier repair — its attachment indices, shifted by the filter, become correct again AND its card is born from the same re-scan); a real named and attached .ics stays a savable chip. No new glyph — the date tile is typographic, statuses are stated in words. Field (2026-08-22 verdict, nine points, fixed on 2026-08-23): (R8, CE verdict — overturns the review's guard) a FORWARDED invitation is an invitation — being on the ATTENDEE list isn't required to reply, whoever forwards it takes on that responsibility; (R6) cancellation is CROSSED — a CANCEL turns off the REQUEST for the same meeting (same event_uid, same account, either arrival order): the ORIGINAL card says "Invitation cancelled", the cancellation isn't orphaned in its new conversation; (R10) the LIST's chip row carries the three gestures — reply without opening (same 24 px chip-buttons, unchanged h2 windowing template), the click doesn't select the row; (R11) a replied-to invitation lends its FACE to the row — subject, sender and preview of the INVITATION, "Accepted / Tentative / Declined / Cancelled" chip — the ONLY case where the list doesn't show the thread's last message, sort order intact; (R12, generic bug flushed out by the field) the "n files" chip of a row sums the WHOLE thread — the head alone was lying as soon as the attachment lived on another message. All through an enrichment pass bounded to the served PAGE — the list's hot query pays nothing. Second pass (2026-08-23 verdict, six points — four finishing touches, fixed within the session): the reply chip replaces the gestures THE INSTANT of the click (optimistic — the journal follows, a failure reverts the previous state and states it); invitation gestures occupy their OWN rank in the row — the other chips (messages, files, pin) live in the rank below and rise up to meet the reply chip when it appears (windowing counts RANKS, constant marginal cost, always two measured templates); buttons AND chips carry their icon — check_circle (meaning "confirmed" widened to "accepted"), cancel (new: decline — never close, which keeps "close"), question_mark (new: tentative — never hourglass_empty, which keeps "scheduled") — and color carries the meaning, borne by the ICON (accent / neutral / alert, text always doubled — A8; pairs already gated); "Cancelled" stays typographic, in alert. "Delete" leaves the thread bar for EACH message (the destructive counterpart of the R4/RETOURS-3 reply bar): one deletes THIS message, the thread stays open if any remains, the echo states the wait as before. A76 glyph tally: 2 new (cancel, question_mark), subset 76 → 78, cache-buster ?v=78. Third pass (2026-08-23): optimism only showed on an already-selected row — the mutation was writing into the windowing's non-reactive pages; the gesture now goes through version, the windowing's invalidation channel, on write as on rewind.
2026-08-23 A77Account removal is stated (PLAN-RETOURS-9, topic 2; CE decision D2 of 2026-08-23). The Settings > Accounts row's button moves from icon alone (delete, meaning carried by aria-label alone) to icon + text "Remove account" — the "Add an account" pattern. The wording stays "remove" (D2, "Delete" from the draft wording refused): the gesture removes the account from Wind, nothing is deleted server-side — that's what the confirmation card already says, and a button shouldn't say anything other than its own confirmation. --muted ink at rest, the alert only shows on hover (A74's drawing kept — permanent red would shout on every healthy account). No new glyph.

An account can carry a chosen name ("Work", "Personal" — 60 characters at most, trimmed spaces, the shell normalizes and is authoritative). The Settings > Accounts row's label is the door: clicking the identity opens the entry card under the row (the marker/removal pattern — pre-filled field, Enter or "Save" applies, clearing the field removes the name). No new glyph: the set has no pencil and A3 forbids reusing one (edit_note means "drafts", edit_square means "write") — the door is textual, like "Reconnect". Surfaces (D4): the name REPLACES the address on the nav tile and in the marker badge's tooltip/aria in the list; in Settings it displays WITH the address (name in weight, address below — it remains the connection truth; likewise the Signature section, where editing the wrong account is costly); D4's onboarding case is moot by construction (no name can exist at first launch — logged, not swept under the rug); in the composer the sender selector says "Name — address" (the value stays the address: the send's functional data doesn't change). The name NEVER touches the From: of outgoing messages — a local label, not an SMTP display name (explicit scope refusal). Local preference nom_compte.{id} (marker/signature pattern), purged with the account on removal — a reused SQLite id never inherits the old identity.
2026-08-24 A79Adoption: this document becomes the reference System, and the UI ships it (PLAN-ELEMENTS; CE decisions D1-D5 of 2026-08-24, V1-V14 closed). D1: the HTML is THE source, hand-edited — the study generator stays frozen as a trace (spikes/direction-elements/v2/), the old System moves to docs/archives/systeme.v1.dc.html, the V series closes, amendments resume here as A-n. Shipped in five steps, each gate-green and validated at the CE visual STOP the same day: E1 the base (17 tokens × 2 themes, --panel removed — 16 uses on --bg —, migration of saved choices: every old -nuit to elements-nuit, everything else to default); E2 the 78 glyphs as inline SVG (lib/icones.js + Icone.svelte, 95 uses converted, the Material font and its README contract dead, "About" mention rewritten — D2: "Wind's original set, drawn after Material Symbols (Google, Apache 2.0)"); E3 shapes (zero radius via the three html tokens, square initials tile, 9 px unread disk, bare-number nav counter, keep mark on pinned rows); E4 the brand (Marque.svelte, two V11 regimes; Hitofude.svelte removed, disk/ring in the status bar); E5 the display register (weight 340 via Segoe UI Variable Display, fallback 400). The gates encode the System: contrast 220 pairs (hairlines 1.49/1.26 and --brand included), coherence — glyph names AND paths in both directions, zero radius literal (the --r-plateforme exception declared), reserved glyphs never placed. D3 (verdict at STOP E2): the three merge families stay differentiated by their current marks (body/lid handle; top band; circle's inner mark) — no redrawing. D4: the reduced masters are shipped, the 16 tier stays V9's debt. Defect found at adoption, repaired: the generator's scope="col" normalization had mangled eleven <thead> tags ("<th scope="col"ead>") — the browser recovered, an automated reader tripped over it; the eleven are repaired, V12's lesson held for this document too. e2e: 124/124; full gate ~1 min 40 s.
2026-08-24 A80The mailbox is stated in words, on the sender's row (PLAN-REPERE-LIGNE; CE decisions D1-D5 of 2026-08-24). The marker badge under the avatar (A74) is replaced by a text block in the header row: in in muted ink (--muted), the marker's glyph at the account's hue (bare stroke, 14 px), then the mailbox label — personalized name (A78) or address. Chief Engineer's reasoning: the sentence reads, and it saves having to permanently remember a color or a logo. In French, the word is sur (D10: the mailbox is a container, not a surface). Three truncation rules, each in one sentence: the time never gets cut (it is the column's reading landmark); the block yields three times faster than the sender and never takes more than a third of the row; both end at the ellipsis, never a hard cut. The third is measured, not chosen: on a 32-character name, at half two sender names cut at the default (400 px pane); at 30% it's the short labels that get cut for nothing at the lower bound; 33 to 36% give the same result — a plateau, hence the third, stated in one word. A8 comes out stronger: the information is carried by a WORD, color and glyph only double it — stronger than what A74 achieved. An account with no marker still states its mailbox (D8: block with no stroke — two markerless accounts stop being indistinguishable, the marker becomes genuinely optional again). The block lives wherever accounts mix — unified inbox and search (A74's D3, unchanged) —, and "mix" is read to the letter (review): a machine with only one account mixes nothing, its block is silent everywhere, list and pane included; the condition rests on the NUMBER of accounts, not merely on the chosen view —, and the reading pane follows the SAME rule as the list (2026-08-25 field verdict): where the row is silent, the card is silent too. D5 said "the same layout in the pane"; the field showed the asymmetry this wording let through — in a single-account view the list said nothing while the pane still spoke — and the same block repeats in the reading pane, behind the sender's name, expanded card and collapsed rows alike (D5). The tooltip gives "label — address"; truncation is CSS only (the whole label stays in the DOM, read by assistive technology); the stroke is aria-hidden: it doubles the word. No new row, no new glyph, no new contrast pair; A44's two templates measured unchanged.
2026-08-24 A81The initials tile leaves the list (PLAN-REPERE-LIGNE; CE decision D9 of 2026-08-24). The row's lead column disappears: the sender's initials said nothing that the name, written out at 10 px above, didn't already say — and they cost 38 px of the pane's 400, to the benefit of the subject, which actually learns something (the mailbox block, A80). The tile survives where it works: the thread's cards (the sender changes from one message to the next there) and the Drafts folder (it states the recipient there). Consequence on V4's phrasing — "the initials avatar becomes a square" — : it stays true of its two remaining uses, and stops holding for the list row.
2026-08-24 A82The marker is a bare glyph; the dot retreats to Settings (PLAN-REPERE-LIGNE; CE decision D6 of 2026-08-24). The solid 20 px dot leaves the navigation: the marker is now drawn right on the background, at the account's hue, 16 px — the size of the folder glyphs in the same column, so that account rows stop being rows apart. Motive: the nav and the list row must carry exactly the same object (D2). What the System loses: V4/V14's statement "the marker dot remains the one other round shape in the whole system" stops holding for screen 02 — measured over the whole window, the only remaining round shape is the disk (row unread, status bar). The disk therefore no longer tells anything but state, what V4 aimed at without reaching. What the System keeps: the dot lives in Settings (account row and choice swatch), where it is a choice dot and not an identity mark — V5 thus holds entirely within its remaining domain. The swatch's 24 hex values now serve twice (dot background, stroke color): they move to --rep-<hue> tokens, one table per polarity, never recopied. Contrasts: the hue as a stroke lands on the same backgrounds as the dot and the measurement table doesn't move (worst case in the swatch: 4.97:1, component threshold 3:1) — no new pair. What is lost, and stated: the colored background gave the marker a presence visible from a distance; a 2-unit stroke at 16 px weighs ~1.3 px — the nav states the account more softly.
2026-08-25 A83Three notches of air between messages (PLAN-ESPACEMENT; CE decisions D1-D3 of 2026-08-25). The list row's vertical spacing becomes adjustable — "Low" (the existing one, PIXEL FOR PIXEL: 13 px padding, row 88), "Medium" (19, 100), "High" (25, 112) —, chosen in Settings > Display, fourth row after "Layout", at A26's exact pattern: native selector dressed at the row's tokens, no new drawing (A15: no new group for one row). Pure UI preference (localStorage, the panes' pattern — the shell has nothing to read from it), restored BEFORE mounting so the first probe already measures the right notch. The notch is set as a TOKEN (--rangee-pad, in a style= on the list frame, --l-nav's pattern): every row takes it in one go, with not one more line of code — the two probes, the waiting row, the flow and the pinned section (which share their template) and the Drafts folder; the hyphen makes it escape the 17-token theme contract, and that's intended (it's a layout dimension, not a color). Air lives in the PADDING, never in a margin nor a row-gap: offsetHeight only sees the border box, and either of those two paths would give 12.375 px per row invisible to the probe — the render would lie while the probe told the truth. The probes become permanent: they stay mounted in a positioned cage and bind via bind:offsetHeight (the hautEpingles pattern); sondees and sonder() die. Measured motive: the probes were withdrawn after a single measurement and sondees was never reset to false — a changed notch would have left the templates frozen on the old height, i.e. a scrollbar off by 13.6% (toward Medium) to 27.3% (toward High) and up to 12,000 px of gap on one jump, i.e. a blank screen. The cage must be positioned, and that isn't decorative: without position:relative it isn't the containing block for the probes' position:absolute, which then anchor on the frame and add up to 85 px of phantom scroll on a short window (the four variants are bench-measured, spikes/espacement/sondes.mjs). The re-anchoring is the inverse of the pinned items': when the height ABOVE the flow moves, pixels keep their meaning and the index gets recomputed; when it's a ROW's height that moves, the index↔pixel conversion changes and it's the top row that gets kept by shifting the scroll. Pre-existing defect fixed along the way (decision D3): the frame's height was read via clientHeight, which isn't a signal — widening the window by more than eight rows left an empty band until the next scroll; bind:clientHeight fixes it, and it had to be done here, this project having made it intermittent and thus unreproducible. Declined (§2.6): the thread and reading pane (the statement says "the center pane"), a dedicated onboarding step (D2 — A75 stays at four steps; the default being the existing state, no one loses anything by not seeing this choice at first launch), and any font or content density. No new glyph, no new color, no new contrast pair.
2026-08-26 A84The list's first page leaves BEFORE the startup probes (PLAN-DEMARRAGE; CE decisions D1-D9 of 2026-08-26). Field finding, cold run on the real database (12.84 GB, 251,524 envelopes, 64 mailboxes): list_category was emitted twelfth and served at 440.6 ms for a clean 28 ms of work — the one command the user was waiting on was the last one served. The cause wasn't a badly written order: prete = true doesn't paint right away, Svelte schedules the flush as a microtask, so the ten calls that followed left before the list was even mounted. An await tick() hands control back to the flush: the list asks for its page first, alone, hence with no rival for the global lock. Nothing is deferred, and that's the rule to hold: chargerNav stays right behind, because its response carries the mailbox block for every row (A80) — delaying it would render rows with no block and then repaint them, and it's the sender that would re-truncate, on every visible row at once. Deferring the probes would manufacture a defect that doesn't exist: they take the same lock as the list, so their response already precedes the rows. Two core fixes accompany this move, invisible on screen but grounded in the same finding: the scanned criterion leaves the catch-up queries (it cost 251k bold-row callbacks over 11.4 GB to protect zero rows — measured on both machines), and the envelopes' date index gains uid, without which SQLite would go fetch the envelope row just to read the polling's uid. Field-measured result, first launch after a machine restart: backfill_status 8,867.8 → 124.9 ms (the service freeze the CE had found), window → full list 1,157.3 → 384.6 ms. What this project doesn't claim: the cumulative latency of the first 60 seconds, dominated by the network, which it doesn't touch. Accepted price (D9): on the first launch after an update, rebuilding the index costs 1.77 s, with no screen — it only reads the 47 MB of envelopes, never the bodies.

Launching is taken over by the application (return checked; the download and its minisign verification stay with the plugin), and the failure follows each surface's existing error path, with no new state: in the banner, erreur.maj flashes and the banner re-arms itself from data already known — never a round trip, whose failure would have refrozen it on "Installing…" with no button; in Settings, the install failure is stated under its true name (erreur.maj, not "Could not check") in front of the "Update available" row, whose "Install" button stays offered — never a dead end. No new component, no new color, no new contrast pair. An account predating the setting is deemed "everything" (D4). Along the way, CE feedback from the visual STOP: the "The server is detected automatically…" note dies — superfluous. e2e 169 → 172.
A103Spring Cleaning — 5th section of Organized Mode (PLAN-HORIZON-NETTOYAGE volet B, D5-D12 settled at STOP 1, two CE visual STOPs on 2026-08-30 — the intro then the sort). The intro: header at the Screener's pattern, CE subtext word for word, the range (3 months → everything, radio pills, default 1 year) and — decision D6, word for word — the SCOPE choice (Inbox only / + Folders / + Folders + Archive / + Archive; Sent, Drafts, Junk, Trash always out of play; Gmail's FULL archive out of scope, stated limit), then "Start cleaning". The sort: the Screener's layout but the rows are GROUPS by sender (name, address, n messages, last subject) — Yes/No holds for the WHOLE group and applies to the range's stock AND to the future (D5: the nettoyage_verdict door sets the routing then logs ONE action per message of the stock within THE verdict's transaction, E3's pattern; server trash, never permanent — D4); the bare click follows the Screener's defaults (D9), the mini ⋯ deviates; the row is the group's DOOR — one enters to SEE its messages (never sorting at the message level, scope refusal); the progress bar at the top states the % of groups processed (the migration gauge's drawing, the % in the text — A52). Senders already routed are excluded (D7, revisable from the Screener history). The session is ONE and PERSISTED (nettoyage_session, D8): bound FROZEN at start, resumed after a restart, "Finish" clears it — the verdicts, though, stay set. e2e 172 → 177.
A104Seven findings from real use — PLAN-RETOURS-14 (D1-D8 settled at STOP 1 on 2026-08-31). The thread bar moves to the TOP and STICKS on scroll (D1): archive / report spam / pin (+ set aside and Move to… in Organized mode) live under the thread's header, position:sticky anchored to the FRAME's scrollport (pane as well as screen 03), opaque --bg background; the "Move to…" menu now opens DOWNWARD; this document's mockups follow, and their outdated "Delete" (moved PER MESSAGE at R8', 2026-08-23) is removed along the way. Settings > Screener gains the FULL list of decisions (D6): every destination (the Screener page's history only shows the screened-out ones), alphabetized, CLIENT-SIDE search, "Reinstate" per row. Kiosk and Registry gain their nav dot (D8): cards NEVER opened (kiosque_lus memory — the page's semantics, not IMAP unseen) for the Kiosk, IMAP unread for the Registry; the Screener already had its own. Em dashes leave all displayed texts (D4): fr/en catalogues, templates ("Name (address)" in the composer and tooltips), core error messages; the "—" glyphs of emptiness (avatar with no letters, unknown version) stay — that's a drawing, not punctuation; catalogs.test.mjs net proven by breaking it. Field the same day (1-7 OK, three feedback items fixed within the session): a Screener YES implies trust (R8) — the verdict ALSO sets the "always show images from this sender" rule (R1's guard table, revocable in Settings > Display; a No touches nothing), set within THE verdict's transaction (poser_verdict — Screener, Move to…, Cleaning, Settings, all paths); the sections' SORT button (R9, form settled in the 2nd field pass) — the button (bare-button drawing "Expand all", right-aligned on the section line) opens a DROPDOWN menu of the four sorts (most recent / oldest / sender A → Z / Z → A, alphabet on the DISPLAYED name, UI language collation), each entry with its glyph — four new glyphs sort_newest/sort_oldest/sort_az/sort_za (decreasing bars + arrow; stacked A/Z + arrow; set 87 → 91, direct CE request) — ONE component (TriSection.svelte + comparateurTri) — Kiosk (Unread AND Previously read, each with its own sort), Registry (title row), Screener history, Cleaning; display only, defaults stay the previous order; "Reinstate" becomes "Edit" in Settings (R10) — the menu re-offers ALL the Screener's rules (the three Yeses, the four Nos) plus "Send back to the screener", the old behavior. mail-core tests 419 → 422, e2e 177 → 187.
A105An exclusive choice in a menu is a menuitemradio (2026-09-01 audit, CE finding at the release build). The four sort menu entries (A104, TriSection.svelte) carried role="menuitem" with aria-checked — an attribute this role doesn't recognize (vite-plugin-svelte a11y warning, silent through two green gates the same day). A8 rule: a menu's checkable entry — a sort, a theme, a single-choice filter — is role="menuitemradio" (exclusive choice) or menuitemcheckbox (toggle), and IT is the one carrying aria-checked; menuitem stays for actions (Move to…, Screen out). The screen reader now says "checked" where it said nothing before. Along the way, the gate stops lying: "zero warnings required" at the ui-v2 build was verified by no one — the hook and gate.ps1 only read the exit code; a [vite-plugin-svelte] warning is now a red, proven by simulating it.
A106The notice slot states the actions the server refused (PLAN-AUDIT-V1 E3, CE decision D2 of 2026-09-01). Before: a journal action (archive, delete, move, mark) refused by the server — missing folder, NO/BAD — blocked the mailbox's WHOLE queue for life, with no word; the user saw their next gestures "taken" and never played. Now the refused action enters QUARANTINE (five transient failures also lead there), the next ones go through, and the slot carries an alert notice: "N action(s) refused by the server — the message stayed where it was." No button (the decision UI — retry, abandon — waits for wave 2); priority right after the send failure, before reconnection: an incident, not information. Same grammar as the send failure (error glyph, alert border). The line re-serves with the send probe (10 s).
A107A body the core failed to serve is stated and can be replayed; "Forward" no longer loads remote images (PLAN-AUDIT-V2 E10, CE decision D8 of 2026-09-02). Before: a core failure loading a body left an EMPTY frame forever in the thread (the reload guard refused any second try until the thread closed). Now the frame carries an incident line — the image-guard grammar (error glyph, text, button): "The message could not be loaded." + Try again, which replays the load. And a FORWARD composition receives the forwarded block at the neutral pixel (BlockRemote): the tracking pixel no longer fires on the "Forward" click; at send time, the block is replaced by the render with its real images — the recipient gets the same message (the §6.4 exception accepted in the field on 2026-08-20 is lifted). The Kiosk, for its part, keeps its cards between two relieves (merge by key, "read" frozen at first serving, later pages kept) and only keeps alive the cards within twelve ranks of the first visible one — a card outside the window leaves a block of its own height.
A108ONE menu for the product — Menu.svelte (PLAN-AUDIT-V2 E11, CE visual STOP of 2026-09-02 on the List, then the seven others: Kiosk, Screener, Cleaning, Registry, section sort, Settings > Screener, the thread's "Move to…"). Closes D-47 and holds A8: eight copies of the drawing (three shadows including one nonexistent --ombre token, three z-indices — 30, 6, 5 —, two item heights, two hover hues) and of the mechanics (one closed on any keystroke, Tab included; none set focus) become one component: floating card in --surface, border, control radius, --shadow shadow, z-index 30 (a menu is the highest object), 32 px items with visible hover and focus in --hover, hairlines and section titles in one copy; anchored to the click coordinates (bounded to the window) or, for the thread, under its trigger. Keyboard: focus lands on the first item at opening, ↑/↓ (wrap), Home/End, Enter plays, Escape and Tab close, clicking outside closes, and focus RETURNS to the trigger. Along the way, D-4 entry: Settings open on their first control; and the product's shortcuts (e, Del, /, Escape…) pressed INSIDE a message body get replayed on the window — a click in a body no longer left them inert.
A109Field STOP 2 of wave 2 — three findings, fixed the same day (PLAN-AUDIT-V2, CE of 2026-09-02, eleven points out of twelve OK). (1) Kiosk, "Always show images" had no effect after ten pages scrolled: the guard called the core then re-served page 0 alone — the merge by key (E10) kept a card past that unchanged. Rule amended: the card re-serves itself, wherever it is, through the same document as the pane (message_body); the sender rule re-serves every card still kept, the core arbitrates (a third party's card re-renders identically). Net: feed-images.spec.js (25 routed senders, the guard of a page-2 card). (2) Forward: a word typed AFTER the block disappeared on send — in a contenteditable, a cursor placed at the end of the body falls INSIDE the last block, here the marked block the send replaces. The forwarded block now ends with an editable blank line: the cursor has an outside, what's typed after it arrives. (3) Outside the UI but visible: the reply_to column (E5) only lived in the CREATE TABLE — on the real database, every watcher pass failed ("no column named reply_to") and "Reply all" refused; migrated via the column list, with the legacy-database test that freshly sown fixtures couldn't replace. Still open in the plan: private RAM after ten Kiosk pages (249 MB across 6 WebView2 processes, budget 200) — measured at three window widths (12 / 5 / 1: +217 / +168 / +96 MB at 160 cards on the bench), D9 (CE, same day): window 5 — at most eleven live iframes; the root cause (one iframe per card, memory retained after return) is D-53; pass 2: 251 MB, of which 132 for the GPU process alone — window size isn't the lever. Pass 2, finding (4): the "Already seen" band overlapped a row, an empty row's worth below — the band lives absolutely positioned per the heights model (h1/h2 probes, A83) while rows stack at their real height; the probes rendered neither the mailbox block (A80, mixed view) nor Organized mode's ⋯ (E4, 24 px centered in a 14 px line) — 6 px less per row, one row short over twenty. Rule: a probe carries everything that gives the real row its height, under the same conditions (net: list-sections.spec.js, the band calibrated on its 2 px gap). CE remark (5): the thread's sticky bar should FLOAT above the message — proposal at the visual STOP: the product's floating object (A108) — surface, border, control radius, --shadow, offset 8 px from the top of the scrollport — accepted on captures, then overturned by the CE in the field (pass 3): three drawings. (a) In the pane, the sort bar (Archive / Report as spam / Pin; Set aside, "Move to…" in Organized mode) is stuck under the thread's header — flat band on the background, closed by a hairline, sticky at the top on scroll (R1 held). (b) On screen 03, its buttons live directly in the scene's header bar, between "← Inbox" and "Compose" — no more bar in the flow. One single component, BarreFil.svelte, two drawings. (c) A message's reply bar (Reply / Reply all / Forward / Delete) floats at the bottom of the message: A108's floating object (surface, border, control radius, --shadow), sticky at the bottom of the scrollport while the message scrolls — 12 px margin with the footer —, in place within the card once its end arrives, at 12/20/16 px from the elevation's edges; tight around its buttons, it doesn't bar the card. CE verdict on captures: "OK as is"; in a narrow pane it stacks (three ranks at 450 px), accepted. Pass 4 in the field: (a') in the pane, the stuck bar stopped 18 px below the visible top — a position:sticky is bounded to the frame's CONTENT edge, under its padding; the frame no longer carries top padding, air is rendered by the thread (--fil-haut); (b') on screen 03, the sort gestures align with the messages column's left edge — the header is a three-track grid whose center track reproduces the column (960 px, 28 px gutters, symmetric scrollbar-gutter on the scene); the return keeps its content width (pass 5: the grid was stretching it to fill its track). Net: thread-bars.spec.js.
A110The wire speaks English; the database keeps its French (PLAN-ENGLISH-SWITCH E5a, CE decisions D15-D17 of 2026-09-03). Five closed vocabularies cross the IPC and are persisted: the category ids, the 12 marker hues, the cleanup scopes, the invitation replies, the sync phases. Rule (D16): the database keeps the French value (D3, debt D-54); the wire, the catalogue keys, the CSS selectors and the test ids carry the English one; the shell maps at the boundary, in one module (wire.rs), never elsewhere. The 24 hex of the marker swatch move from --rep-<teinte> to --mk-<hue> with the twelve English family names (red, orange, ochre, olive, green, pine, blue, indigo, violet, magenta, pink, brown) — the values do not move, the contrast table does not move; the data-teinte attribute keeps its name until the DOM contract switches (E5d), its VALUES are English from here. Four glyphs of the set are renamed with the views they name: feed, paper_trail, screener, cleanup (drawings untouched). The IPC keys follow: 18 command parameters and ~45 payload fields in English (title, hue, lastEpoch…), the six bulk-gesture words too. Nothing visible changes: the French catalogue is delivered word for word, only its value-derived keys move (boite.inbox, repere.teinte.blue, inv.puce_accepted…).
A111English is the reference language of the interface (PLAN-ENGLISH-SWITCH E5b, Chief Engineer decision D4 of 2026-09-02; ADR 0016 amended in place). Rule: a key missing from the active catalogue falls back to the ENGLISH text; the first launch speaks English unless the system language is French (lib/language.js, one pure decision, e2e/language.test.mjs); the shell composes the notifications in English by default (Lang::from_pref). The French catalogue is delivered word for word (D3), only its keys are English (glossary §5.4). Nothing else visible changes: the UI code, its 43 files and its identifiers are in English, its comments too; the DOM contract (test ids, classes, data-* names, seams) keeps its French until E5d, the four remaining CSS tokens until E5c. Two persisted UI preferences migrate at read, without a reset: the list pane width (wind-largeurs, key liste → list) and the row spacing (wind-espacement, faible|moyen|eleve → low|medium|high).

A113The DOM contract speaks English (PLAN-ENGLISH-SWITCH E5d, Chief Engineer decisions D15 and D18-D21 of 2026-09-03). A114The e2e layer speaks English (PLAN-ENGLISH-SWITCH E6a, Chief Engineer decisions D22-D26 of 2026-09-03).
